From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme-payments.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + DPA questions (Acme Payments)

Ben —

Thanks for the recap. A couple specifics from Legal that we need clarified before we can proceed to our procurement team: 

1) Controller / Processor: In our view Acme Payments will be the Controller and Redwood the Processor for any personal data processed for the payment matching use case. Can you confirm Redwood accepts that role and will sign the DPA reflecting processor obligations?

2) Subprocessors: please provide a current list of subprocessors (hosting, logging/monitoring, analytics) and confirm your process for notifying us of new subprocessors and a minimum notice period.

3) Breach notice: what is your standard breach notification timeframe? Our policy requires notification within 72 hours of detection for incidents affecting personal data.

4) Data residency & retention: we need to ensure payment PII remains in the US by default, and need retention controls to auto-delete customer-provided PII after 90 days unless otherwise agreed. Is that supported?

5) Logging & audit: we need clarity on what logs you retain (request/response, metadata only vs full payloads), how long logs are retained, and whether we can request audit exports for SOC2/compliance reviews.

If you can respond to these items in a short written note (or point us to the specific DPA sections), we can loop Procurement in.

Regards,
Tom Alvarez
Senior Counsel, Privacy | Acme Payments

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme-payments.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Sara Lim <sara.lim@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + DPA questions (Acme Payments)

Hi Tom / Sara —

Thanks for the clear list — below are concise answers and references to the DPA (attached). I've also attached the current subprocessors export. If you'd like, we can add a short addendum to reflect the 90-day retention requirement for your projects.

1) Controller / Processor
- Redwood acknowledges we will act as a Processor for customer-provided personal data related to the payment-matching integration. The attached DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf) is drafted to reflect Processor obligations (security, confidentiality, purpose limitation). We can sign as Processor.

2) Subprocessors
- Attached: subprocessors_current_2026-03.csv contains our present subprocessors (hosting: AWS US-EAST-1; monitoring/logging: Datadog; analytics: Segment; SSO: Okta).
- Notice: our DPA includes a notification process for new subprocessors. We provide advance notice by email and offer a termination right where required by applicable law. Typical notification window is 30 days; we can discuss a contractual notice period if you need longer.

3) Breach notice
- We commit to notifying customers of security incidents affecting personal data without undue delay and will provide initial notification within 72 hours of becoming aware, consistent with industry practice and your request. Follow-up communications include impact analysis and remediation steps.

4) Data residency & retention
- By default, hosting and processing for your account can be restricted to the US (we run regional partitions). We support data residency controls and will provision US-only processing for Acme Payments.
- Retention: Redwood supports configurable retention policies. We can configure automatic deletion of customer-provided PII after 90 days post-ingest for the payment-matching dataset; we can add an addendum to the DPA to capture this requirement and the deletion verification process.

5) Logging & audit
- Scope: We retain request metadata (timestamps, request IDs, model variant, latency, tokens) by default. We do not retain full user-provided payloads unless explicitly enabled by the customer for debugging or caching.
- Retention: default logs retention is 180 days; we can extend/shorten based on contract.
- Audit exports: we can provide SOC2 reports and custom audit exports (redacted where appropriate) under an NDA / audit schedule; we can also provide short-term export snapshots for compliance reviews.

Next steps:
- I attached the DPA and subprocessors list. If Acme wants the 90-day deletion requirement codified, we can prepare a short addendum and route for signature (or include in the SOW).
- If Tom / Sara want a technical follow-up with Neha to review logging/encryption details (KMS/HSM, at-rest/in-transit, key management options), we can schedule a 30-min call this week.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf, subprocessors_current_2026-03.csv
